body:
**The year he leaves Pennsylvania, quits smoking for the third recorded time,
reads his own archive, and is still voting for Cory Booker ten months before
becoming a socialist.**

2019 is thin — 57 posts — and almost every one of them is load-bearing for
something else in the corpus.

## 3 March: "Au revoir Pennsylvania. Adiós Trump country."

One line, no elaboration, and it is the only dated departure from Fayette
County anywhere in the archive.

`wiki/self/location-history` records an address-level blind window that the
2013, 2014 and 2016 pages have now filled with presence in Western PA. This
closes the other end of it: he was there, and on **3 March 2019** he left, and
he framed the leaving politically — *"Trump country"* — rather than
practically. Later in the year the state is a destination rather than a home:
**10 October**, *"today i bought a can of skoal to prepare me for a weekend in
Pennsylvania."*

Where he went is not stated here. *"Miss u nyc"* (2017-08-15) and *"reasons i
moved to nyc"* (below) are the only nearby evidence and neither is a current
address. This is a gap the page names rather than fills.

## The nicotine pattern, now stated by him, at n=3

`wiki/self/twitter/2010` records a tobacco quit via e-cigarette on 13 December
2010; `wiki/self/twitter/2011` shows it lasted at most three weeks. On
**9 October 2019** he does it again, and this time explains the logic himself:

> *"one reason i started vaping is because i felt like a piece of shit for
> exposing my animals to smoke. the other is because i could replace the
> constant taste of burnt tobacco with strawberry or other flavors that aren't
> terrible"*
>
> *"it's anecdotal af but the health benefits of switching were immediately
> obvious. my lungs don't feel like they're full of fluid anymore and the
> 'wheezing' thing doesn't plague me like it did for 5 years while smoking"*

**Replace the delivery system, keep the molecule, and report the health
benefit** — stated in his own words, nine years after doing exactly the same
thing with the same substance, and nine years after the corpus's other instance
of the same structure. `wiki/health/chemical-architecture` catalogues nicotine
as a ritual regulator; this is the mechanism by which the regulator is
preserved through every attempt to remove it.

He defends the arrangement politically too, on **12 September**, against the
flavour ban: *"i'm sure there's some super good reason to wait until paragraph
8 before bringing up that the #flavorban is a response to a completely
unrelated issue."*

And on **10 October**, immediately after: *"today i bought a can of skoal"* and
*"apparently one dose of skoal is equivalent to smoking 327 cigarettes because
i feel like i'm about to black tf our."* A fourth delivery system, tried within
a day of the third being praised.

## 9 October: he read his own archive

> *"reading through my old tweets from like 2009 and the only thing i can
> relate to or recognize is all the pot talk."*

Seven years before this wiki existed, Dan ran the same operation on the same
corpus and reported the result: **continuity of one habit, discontinuity of
everything else.** It is worth setting beside what these nineteen pages
actually found, because he is close to right and wrong in an interesting place
— the *vocabulary* and *affiliations* change completely, and the *method*
(anomaly detection, the on/off self-verdict, the announced-then-unshipped
project) does not change at all. He could see the surface change and not the
structural constancy, which is the ordinary condition of looking at yourself
from inside.

The same day, 24 September: *"i've been on twitter for 11 years, which is more
than the number of interesting or insightful tweets i've produced."*

## Still a liberal, in October 2019

The August 2020 self-narration is ten months away. The politics here are
impeachment politics, consumed as procedural drama and produced as comedy.

The **27 September whistleblower thread** is six consecutive posts imagining
the whistleblower's domestic life — *"what did the whistleblower have for
dinner tonight? did they order in? i bet they had leftovers because they ate
lunch late and haven't had an appetite"*, and a closing note that they should
get rid of *"WHSLBLWR"* vanity plates. On **4 December**, watching the
Judiciary Committee: *"Prof Karlan is a fucking OG loc GANGSTER"*, *"Matt Gaetz
is a shitlord"*, *"okay so this is just a filibuster"*, *"i miss the intel
committee."*

And on **18 October**: *"i'm voting cory booker because i have a $6 bet that if
he runs against trump in the general election he will be called 'googly eye
cory' a bunch of times."*

It is a joke, and jokes are still made out of the available material. Nothing
in 2019 mentions Sanders, socialism, class, labour, healthcare or capitalism.
On **2 October** he addresses *"moderate conservatives who elected this guy as
a symbolic ultimatum"* — a person still arguing across the aisle rather than
outside the room.

**Ten months later he is a democratic socialist.** That is the single most
useful thing this page establishes: `wiki/mind/synthesis/2020-left-turn` dates
the conversion to a specific day, and 2019 shows the state immediately prior
was not a partly-converted one. The turn is as abrupt as that page says, and it
follows three years of liberalism rather than a slow leftward drift.

He is also, on **16 January**, still a comedy free-speech absolutist: *"The
recent joke shaming of Louis CK is so fucking disturbing. You don't have to
agree with the material to appreciate the essence of what a joke is."*
`wiki/interests/opie-and-anthony` dates his move away from that position to
28 March 2022; this is the last dated instance of the old one.

## The record collection is gone

On **12 October**, six posts:

> *"the best thing about my record collection which included first press brand
> new, signed tttyg clear blue vinyl, is/was a real boy, first press rise or
> die trying, first press mf doom etc etc is that i don't have it anymore i
> guess"*
> *"fun fact i bought two of those deja entendu records and sold one for $900
> in 2014."*
> *"i had a pre release version of late registration for def jam a&r 7 of 20"*
> *"but the resale value and the incredible cost is not nearly the biggest loss
> i feel about these treasures getting sold as $1 bin throwaway vinyl"*

**Somebody else sold them, and sold them as junk.** He does not say who, when,
or under what circumstances, and the sarcasm (*"i can't stop winning"*) is
carrying the whole weight. A collection with a documented $900 single sale and
a numbered promotional pressing went out at a dollar a record.

This is a real loss event with no date, no agent and no context anywhere in the
corpus, and it is filed here as an **open gap** rather than a finding. It sits
in the same period as the Pennsylvania departure, seven months earlier, which
is a proximity worth checking against any household or storage record that
turns up.

## One retrospective worth keeping

**13 October**, on the 2010 move:

> *"reasons i moved to nyc  1 punk as fuck 2 no driving 3 nobody wants small
> talk while checking out 4 availability of sex workers"*
> *"^sort by( importance: low to high)"*

The second post inverts the first, which makes the fourth item the first
reason. It is a joke, told nine years later, by somebody who chose to tell it —
and `wiki/mind/psychosexual/arrangement-history` is the page it belongs to.
Whether it is true is not settleable here; that he said it is.

## What would change this reading

The "still a liberal in October 2019" claim rests on absence — nothing about
class, labour or socialism in 57 posts — in a year that is spreadsheet-backed
but not proven exhaustive. The record-collection loss has no date and no
agent, and any of the three could turn out to be him. And the Pennsylvania
departure is one line: it says he left, not where he went or for how long, and
he is back in the state for a weekend seven months later.
